en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the effort needed by Ifugao farmers to carry heavy loads up the steep mountains.
The wooden wheels of a traditional Cebu kalesa use the wheel and axle principle to multiply the horse's pulling force.
Rough abaca ropes provide high friction, preventing them from slipping when Filipino fishermen tie their small bangka boats to wooden docks.
Earth's gravity pulls a falling coconut straight down toward the soil, regardless of whether it drops from a tree in Quezon or Davao.
The black sand beaches of Ilocos contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that can attract small iron filings.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts natural underground heat from volcanoes into the electricity that lights up Filipino homes.
Fireflies in the mangroves of Palawan produce bioluminescence, a chemical reaction that creates cold light without generating any heat.
During the tinikling dance, the striking bamboo poles create a loud clacking sound because the vibrating wood pushes the surrounding air molecules.
When cooking adobo, heat transfers from the hot metal of the aluminum pot to the liquid soy sauce through direct conduction.
A fast river in Bukidnon possesses high kinetic energy, which local microhydro power plants convert into usable electrical energy.
Sugarcane grown in the fields of Negros Occidental stores chemical energy in its sweet juice, which can be processed into bioethanol fuel.
Filipino farmers use a sturdy wooden lever to easily lift heavy sacks of harvested palay from the ground.
